title: The Loves of Jubayr bin Umayr and Lady Budur

keywords: the loves of jubayr bin umayr and lady budur
full_text:
Jubayr bin Umayr, a wealthy young nobleman of Basra, had wed the peerless Lady Budur, daughter of the city’s chief judge. For a year, their home was an arbor of joy, song, and poetry.

Yet in a moment of thoughtless haste, provoked by an idle remark during a banquet, Jubayr swore a rash oath that estranged them. Lady Budur, wounded by his pride, returned to her father’s palace, refusing to look upon his face or receive his letters.

Stricken with remorse, Jubayr realized that earthly wealth is cold ash when separated from the soul’s beloved. He abandoned his fine apparel, donned the patched robe of a penitent, and wandered along the banks of the Euphrates, reciting poems of lamentation and longing.

The wise vizier of Basra, observing Jubayr's sincere sorrow, resolved to act as an ambassador of peace. He arranged a literary gathering at his garden estate, inviting the chief judge and his daughter behind the embroidered silk screens.

The vizier invited Jubayr to recite his verses before the company. Jubayr stood before the assembly, his voice trembling with genuine remorse, reciting poems of how pride shatters the mirror of joy and how humble forgiveness is the greatest virtue of the soul.

Behind the screen, Lady Budur listened, her heart melting as she recognized the depth of his transformation. She sent forth an inscribed crystal cup filled with fragrant pomegranate sherbet, with a verse answering: 'The heart that repents in truth has already built a garden where love blossoms anew.'

The lovers were joyously reconciled before the assembly, having learned that forgiveness is a stronger cement for a home than any youthful vow.
moral: Patience, repentance, and mutual forgiveness heal the deepest rifts between loving hearts.
